draft.title: Inflation and the cost of living
card: Inflation is a general rise in prices over time. It is usually given as a percentage a year. If inflation is 5%, a basket of goods that cost $100 now costs $105.
When prices rise, the same income buys less. This is a fall in purchasing power, and it makes the cost of living higher.
Compare a pay rise with inflation. If pay rises by less than inflation, the worker can buy less than before. This is a cut in real terms, even though the dollar amount went up.
Example: Sam's pay rises 2% while inflation is 5%. Pay is up 2% but prices are up 5%, so Sam is worse off by about 3 percentage points in real terms.
draft.remember: Compare the pay rise with inflation. If pay rises by less, real income falls.

a.q: Ella gets a 2% pay rise in a year when inflation is 4%. What happens to her pay in real terms?
opts: It falls, because prices rose faster than her pay
It rises, because her pay went up by 2%
It stays the same, because both numbers rose
It rises, because inflation is higher than her pay
a.why: Prices rose by 4% but her pay rose by only 2%, so she can buy less than before. Her pay went up in dollars, which is the tempting mistake, but real terms means comparing it with prices.
a.clue: Compare the size of the pay rise with the rise in prices.

b.q: Inflation is 3% for the year. Which pay rise leaves a worker with more buying power than before?
b.why: Pay must rise by more than prices for buying power to grow. A 5% rise beats 3% inflation. A 3% rise only keeps up with prices, so buying power stays the same, not higher.
b.clue: Which pay rise is bigger than the rise in prices?

a.best: It falls, because prices rose faster than her pay
